profile.campus: Digital Fortress Meadowville Technology Park campus, Chesterfield County VA (88-100 acres)
profile.reading: Digital Fortress: Richmond occupies a wholesale data center campus at 1401 Meadowville Technology Parkway, Richmond, Virginia, in Chesterfield County's Meadowville Technology Park, equidistant from Ashburn, Virginia's Data Center Alley and Virginia Beach's transatlantic cable landing stations. Digital Fortress's own dedicated wholesale Richmond page, fetched fresh, describes a 242,000 square foot building on a 100 acre private campus, comprising 18,270 square feet of ready built out white space in a single data hall plus 196,625 square feet of shell and core space for future expansion, with 4.2 megawatts of current power capacity scalable to 25 megawatts, designed to Tier III standards with fully redundant N+1 concurrently maintainable mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, and Gold LEED certification. A May 21, 2021 unveiling article on the Meadowville Technology Park's own site describes an 88 acre campus figure and a 250,000 square foot LEED Gold building, both broadly consistent with the operator's own more precise figures, and states the campus supports up to 100 megawatts of total on-site power capacity, with the initial 4.1 megawatt facility expandable to 25 megawatts within 20 weeks of a customer commitment. That same coverage describes Digital Fortress as operating since 1994, having grown from nine facilities nationwide to include this Richmond site, offering colocation and cloud access services to enterprises across states including Washington, Oregon, Colorado, and Illinois, consistent with this registry's other Digital Fortress rows. The campus includes a private road entrance, a visitor screening building, Class A office space for up to 120 employees, a dedicated loading dock, and redundant fiber connectivity with diverse demarcation points. Digital Fortress is a Chirisa Investments portfolio company.

reading.body:
Digital Fortress: Richmond is a colocation facility in Chesterfield County, Virginia. No power capacity, rack count, cooling specification, or other IT infrastructure figure is published by the operator. The facility's own specification page on the operator's website returns a 404 error. Without published power or density data, this campus cannot be assessed for AI scaling relevance.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish power capacity totaling 1,375 megawatts. This facility is ranked 24th by published capacity among those sites, placing it below the state's published baseline and indicating no disclosed power figure.

The operator's own homepage confirms a Richmond location and accepts quote requests but does not disclose specifications for this site. Any assessment of this campus's role in AI infrastructure would require the operator to publish power capacity, IT load, or cooling specifications, which are not currently available.
